item.description:
CZI and LIF pixel decoding, physical calibration, and cache-provenance fixes

  • Mixed-depth and float/BGRA pixel decoding (.czi and .lif). Leica .lif mixed 8-bit/16-bit channels decode at each channel's declared bit depth with lossless dtype promotion, and Zeiss .czi PixelType 8 (Bgr96Float), PixelType 9 (Bgra32), and mixed-depth SubBlocks decode with per-SubBlock DV header validation.
  • Full-range integer RGB windows, channel identity mapping, and LIF calibration. uint16/uint32 RGB images use full data-range display windows, sparse .czi channels map by Channel:N ID, and .lif physical step calibration divides span by NumberOfElements - 1.
  • Plane-isolated T/P/Z annotations and verified cache reuse. Confocal annotations are isolated per (T, P, Z) plane with non-destructive 2.6.1 migration, and existing .nd2svs caches validate source fingerprint, selected plane, channel labels/dtypes, and physical calibration before reuse.

Interactive Z-stack, time-series, and multi-series navigation for Zeiss CZI (.czi) and Leica LIF (.lif)

  • Interactive Z-axis slider (#z-knob) for confocal .czi and .lif Z-stacks. Confocal .czi and .lif Z-stack acquisitions now open directly in interactive multi-plane navigation mode with the right-hand Z-axis slider (#z-knob), home-plane indicator, physical micrometer Z-step offset readout, and F autofocus.
  • Time-series, LambdaScan & multi-series container navigation. Multi-frame time-series and spectral LambdaScan .czi / .lif files expose the bottom timeline scrubber (#t-track), and multi-series .lif containers with uniform series dimensions open as a position grid with instant series switching.

Zeiss CZI (.czi) and Leica LIF (.lif) plane scan & confocal support

  • Zeiss CZI plane scan & confocal support (.czi). Open 8-bit/16-bit/float32 fluorescence and 24-bit/48-bit RGB .czi acquisitions (uncompressed, Zstd0, Zstd1 HiLo, JPEG-XR, JPEG, LZW, and ApoTomeRaw) with automatic .nd2svs OME-Zarr pyramid caching, multi-tile mosaic stitching, and Z-plane selection (mid, max projection, or integer Z index).
  • Leica LIF fluorescence & confocal support (.lif). Open LAS AF / LAS X .lif multi-series containers (8-bit/16-bit/float32 fluorescence, LIGHTNING deconvolved 16-bit Z-stacks, spectral LambdaScan series, and RGB snapshots) with .nd2svs pyramid caching, physical micrometer calibration, ATLConfocalSettingDefinition objective magnification, and fluorophore/LUT channel colors.
  • Metadata, LUTs, annotations & ROI export. Full multi-channel LUT window/gamma adjustment and persistence, sidecar ROI annotations, and native-value TIFF/ND2 and rendered PNG/JPEG/SVG/Astromap ROI exports work seamlessly on .czi and .lif slides.

Update card across slide opens, translucent tracing windows, multi-window dialog targeting

  • Update card across slide opens. Opening the first slide from the start window keeps an active update offer or download visible in the bottom-right update card instead of cancelling it, and hides the start window's update button while the card is shown.
  • Translucent tracing windows. Closing a slide tab closes its translucent tracing window automatically, and reopening a slide after a cancelled update allows the translucent viewer to open again.
  • Slide opening feedback. Unsupported or missing files keep their error message visible on the start window and after update recovery, and the opening progress tab remains visible until the new slide tab appears.
  • Multiple windows. File dialogs and title-bar zoom actions target the active viewer window instead of always using the first window.

Windows external drives and paths, reliable multi-slide opening, session lock cleanup

  • Windows external drives and paths. Launching from an exFAT or FAT32 drive no longer logs false download-mark warnings, and tab titles and sidecar status messages show only the file name for Windows paths.
  • Opening multiple slides. Dropping additional files while the first slide is opening keeps every file in the queue, and concurrent conversions each keep their own progress tab.
  • Session locks and sidecars. Closed or terminated windows clean up their .window-live lock files, and legacy annotation sidecar migration skips symbolic links.
  • Update card and recovery. Both the start page and open slides use the bottom-right translucent update card on macOS, release notes remain accessible while an update downloads, manual update retries lock their buttons until the check finishes, and slides can be reopened by drag-and-drop if an update is cancelled after teardown.

Windows startup fix, tidier download, compact update card

  • Windows startup fix. The viewer starts from a ZIP extracted with Windows Explorer. It no longer stops with "Failed to resolve Python.Runtime.Loader.Initialize".
  • Tidier Windows download. The extracted folder shows only nd2wsi-viewer.exe, _internal and READ-ME.txt. The ZIP holds about 40% fewer files.
  • Compact update card. Updates show a few summary lines. Select Details to read the full notes.
  • macOS updates. Installing an update no longer waits indefinitely for a stuck slide read. A cancelled update leaves the window in a clear state, and the app declares macOS 14 as its minimum.

Translucent update card and refined theme

  • Theme. Dark #191919 and light #FFFFFF backgrounds share consistent translucent surfaces. The toolbar and status bar show essential image details. Hover over the checkmark for auto-save, cache and calibration details; orange indicates a problem.
  • Update card on macOS. Updates appear in one card with bullet-point release notes and download progress. When ready, Install and relaunch is on the left and Cancel is on the right. The card also shows save/export waits and errors. The standard Sparkle window remains the fallback.
  • Update check on Windows. The start page's update check uses the same card and opens the download for this PC's build in your browser.
  • Cloud icon. The toolbar's cloud icon is now the viewer's own drawing, so the icon credit under Slide Info is gone.
  • Annotations panel. Its status line no longer shows the internal annotation file name.
  • Windows support. The Windows build lists Windows 11 (x64, and ARM64 through x64 emulation) as its supported target; Windows 10 is not tested.

Safer annotations and caches, 16-bit PNG, faster plates

  • An annotation file the viewer cannot draw is refused before it replaces your marks, and a typed label survives clicking another mark.
  • 16-bit grayscale PNG files keep their stored values in display, pixel readouts and TIFF export.
  • A window opened after the Mac slept no longer removes another window's cache build.
  • The tracing window ignores the image's rotate, flip, zoom and pan keys, so it stays aligned with the main viewer.
  • Plate thumbnails fill about 5 times faster, and cached slides serve more tiles per second.

Safer Windows close, faster display and export

  • Windows now waits for annotation, LUT and export work to be saved before a window closes, as macOS does; an unresponsive viewer can still be closed after an explicit confirmation.
  • Tile compositing is 4–5 times faster with bit-identical colours.
  • Panning over thousands of annotations stays smooth.
  • Native TIFF export from reduced levels reads each channel once; files are byte-identical.

Auto-save status and consolidated viewer internals

  • A green check beside the scale bar shows that your marks and LUT edits were written; hover it for the time since the last save. Failed saves retry every minute, and conflicts still use the recovery notice.
  • Closing or reloading a browser-mode tab now flushes pending saves first.
  • Annotation saving, viewer coordinate calculations and pyramid reduction are consolidated into shared modules with fixed reference values; stored annotation, correction and LUT formats and pixel rounding are unchanged.
  • Legacy BF-free models remain readable, covered by a frozen compatibility fixture; historical beta build recipes moved under packaging/legacy.

Astromapper, large JPEGs and linked-view alignment

  • Select a numbered Astromapper ROI, then use Left and Right to review adjacent regions without changing magnification.
  • Open JPEGs up to 512 megapixels at their stored resolution, subject to a memory check before decoding.
  • ROI import errors now identify invalid rows and mismatched reference dimensions while preserving existing annotations.
  • Shift-drag adjusts one linked view's offset; the updated guide illustrates four-point manual alignment using corresponding histological features.

This release adds a translucent reference window and improves annotation exchange, ROI navigation and cache creation on external drives.

  • Translucent reference: use the cloud button to keep the current image above other apps. Adjust opacity, pan and zoom, or lock the window. Resizing changes the field of view while preserving image scale.
  • ROI navigation: a matching whole-image JPG and Astromapper TXT adds numbered ROI boxes and previous/next navigation to the reference window. Clicking an ROI number in the main Astromapper panel now centres it without changing the current zoom, including while a zoom animation is running.
  • More workspace: collapse the top tools, and use ⌘N / Ctrl+N to open a separate viewer window.
  • GeoJSON import: bring points, lines, polygons with holes and multipart annotations into the open image. Imports append to existing marks and preserve image coordinates and feature metadata. Invalid or unsupported features reject the whole import. QuPath ellipses, geometry collections and non-default planes remain unsupported; see the annotation guide.
  • External-drive cache fix: new viewing caches on macOS exFAT volumes no longer fail because SQLite sees the newly created database file as having moved.
  • Updated documentation: the README and user guide now show the current UI, explain LUT persistence and distinguish shading illustrations from the development validation results.

The original scans, saved annotations and LUT preferences are preserved. Shading illustrations use the current method with identical display settings before and after correction; they are not independent biological validation.

The macOS app requires Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. It is ad-hoc signed and uses signed Sparkle updates; it is not notarized. The Windows portable ZIP contains an x64 app and supports Windows 11 ARM64 through x64 emulation.

On macOS only the image layer changes opacity. Windows applies whole-window opacity, including to controls and ROI outlines. Keep the source tab open while using its translucent reference, and use the corresponding uncropped JPG in the same orientation when importing ROI coordinates.

• Fixed C, E and A panel shortcuts, plus image flip and 90-degree turn shortcuts with annotations following the image.
  • Fixed whole-slide TIFF export at the selected resolution, including half size.
  • Periodic shading correction fits a repeating illumination function independently for supported FITC and CY3 channels. BF and DAPI remain unchanged.
  • Added Astromapper ROI TXT import, JPG and TXT ZIP export, optional annotated PDF reports, and direct JPG annotation.

Apple silicon, macOS 14 or later; ad-hoc signed and not Developer ID notarized.

Rank1 shading correction and panel shortcuts

Shading Correction now defaults to Rank1 (BF-free) for supported FITC and CY3 channels. BF and DAPI stay unchanged. Existing corrections remain readable, and BF-guided stays available as a manual choice.

Panel shortcuts now work consistently from the tab toolbar and active slide, with held-key repeat suppression and editable-field protection.

Original slides, annotations, saved LUTs and native-value exports retain their preservation rules. This macOS Apple silicon build is ad-hoc signed and is not Developer ID notarized.

• Maintenance release: shared reader lifetime, tile caching and RGB level access are organized in a common module.
  • Slide Info uses one reader-selection path for embedded images and previews.
  • Existing viewing features, pixel calculations, source checks, annotations, saved LUTs and storage formats are unchanged.

Open SDPC slides and their original embedded photographs

Version 2.3.0 adds supported SQ/SDPC HEVC slides alongside Nikon ND2 and Aperio SVS. The decoder is included, and SDPC tiles are read on demand without whole-slide conversion or a pixel-pyramid cache.

Slide Info now shows the source-embedded photographs and thumbnail. Click an image to enlarge it within the inspector. Images without a verified label/macro identifier use neutral names in their source order.

The toolbar uses a dashed-square Export button, a pencil for Annotate, and icon-only Info. Channels uses ⌘C, Annotate uses ⌘A, Export uses E, and Info keeps ⌘I. Normal text editing retains copy and select-all behavior.

Rectangular tiles, image edges and physical calibration are retained. Native TIFF ROI export preserves decoded RGB, not samples lost during the source's lossy compression. Original slides, annotations and saved LUTs retain their existing preservation rules.

Corresponding decoder sources and third-party licenses accompany the release. Support is limited to the validated HEVC whole-slide variant; JPEG whole-slide SDPC and vendor colour-correction emulation are not included. The macOS app remains ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID notarized.

Stronger local shading correction

Shading Correction now evaluates FITC, CY3 and brightfield. An adaptive fallback supports scans where the original method lacks enough repeated fields. Local measurements restore correction strength while trough-depth limits reduce dark-to-bright reversal. Unsupported channels remain unchanged.

Existing saved corrections remain in place after updating. Use Revoke, then Apply, to refit them with 2.2.1. Both operations require the original ND2.

DAPI, original pixel readouts, native ND2/TIFF exports, source files, annotations and saved LUTs remain unchanged. Adaptive and BF-corrected caches require version 2.2.0 or later.

Improvement varies by location. Validation within one development acquisition does not establish biological preservation or performance on independent acquisitions. Apple silicon, macOS 12 or later; ad-hoc signed and not notarized.

Shading Correction estimates repeating illumination shading in supported stitched ND2 scans and replaces the existing .nd2svs viewing pyramid. The correction remains saved after reopening. Review the estimated time, then Continue to prepare it with progress and cancellation. Revoke rebuilds the original viewing pyramid from the source ND2.

Correction targets FITC/CY3 using same-scan BF evidence and recorded camera geometry. The original ND2, native ND2/TIFF exports, pixel readouts, annotations and saved LUTs retain their original values or settings. PNG, JPEG and SVG exports use the saved correction. Unsupported or unsuccessful attempts leave a visible explanation that correction was not applied. Inspect the result, especially at tissue boundaries; visible shading can remain when validation fails.

Cancellation or failure before the final replacement leaves the current cache untouched. If a saved replacement cannot be activated immediately, the valid cache is retained and the viewer asks you to reopen the slide. Corrected caches require version 2.1.15 or later; the format guard in older viewers leaves them untouched and requests an update.

macOS Finder document-opening handlers are bound before native window creation to accept documents arriving during startup.

Remember the last-viewed LUT for each file

The standard viewer restores each file's last-used channel minimum, maximum and gamma, even after restarting the app. Preferences are stored locally and separately for each source, without changing image data or annotations. The opt-in Metal viewer's independent controls are not persisted.

Compact LUT editing control

The Channels & LUTs toolbar replaces the large gold Type LUT button with a compact, borderless pencil icon from the same Fluent set as the adjacent copy and paste controls.

Hover over edit, copy or paste for one second to see a short description of its function.

Raw image values, annotations and the cache format are unchanged.

Precise LUT entry and transfer

Enter channel minimum, maximum and gamma with Type LUT. Copy LUTs between windows and paste only uniquely matching, compatible channel names. Raw pixels and annotations are unchanged.

Compact toolbar icons show a green check and Copied! after successful copying. macOS title-bar dragging uses the native Cocoa operation, including after display changes.

Automatic ND2 contrast

  • ND2 opens with automatic contrast and a fitted LUT graph, with reduced sensitivity to rare bright pixels.
  • Manual edits take priority; full-range histograms and native pixel values remain available. RGB Auto uses a shared window.
  • Plate time, Z, playback, autofocus and cache-status controls have a dedicated, directly tested controller.
  • Floating panels have reachable resize edges and a visible corner grip, with recovery after interrupted drags.

Readable light-mode action buttons

The annotation editor's Done button now has a blue background with white text in light appearance, including SVS viewing. The same correction applies to the ND2 export button.

Dark appearance, annotation saving, image rendering and scientific exports are unchanged. Apple silicon, macOS 12 or later.

Full-screen tabs

Slide tabs now remain visible and usable when entering full-screen with the green macOS window button. Leaving full-screen restores the original window size and inline controls without reloading slides.

Existing RGB ND2 controls, annotations, measurements, calibrated SVG export and the Metal option are unchanged.

nd2wsi-viewer 2.1.8

Maintenance release with matching macOS and Windows source versions.

  • Reuse shared window-launch setup and remove unused cache-lock and rectangle helpers.
  • Keep slow session writes outside launch admission, preventing false update-in-progress errors during simultaneous window starts.
  • Retain independent RGB brightfield controls, calibrated scale-bar exports and existing viewing behavior.
  • No image-cache format, original pixel data or annotation migration.

Standard viewing remains the default; compatible Apple silicon slides can opt in to Metal.

RGB brightfield channel controls

  • RGB ND2 and SVS images expose Red, Green and Blue histograms and LUT controls.
  • Each component has independent display range, gamma and visibility.
  • The brightfield light theme and original default RGB appearance are preserved.
  • Rendered tiles and PNG/JPEG/SVG exports use the same channel settings.

Original pixels, calibration, raw export and annotations are unchanged.

Precise contrast and dependable controls

  • Fractional LUT windows retain precision through display and rendering.
  • Z navigation and offsets follow the recorded stack direction.
  • Checkbox and comparison controls respect keyboard focus.
  • Histogram failures recover automatically or offer Retry.
  • Uncached plate windows show their state and stop idle polling.

Includes the opening, automatic-update and recovery fixes from 2.1.5.

Reliable opening and recovery

  • Keyboard shortcuts work immediately after a slide opens.
  • Automatic updates resume and installation waits for other viewer windows.
  • Annotation conflicts can close after explicit recovery-draft preservation.
  • Sparse plate wells retain separate cells; interrupted cache writes recover safely.

Versions 2.1.1–2.1.4 need one manual upgrade to resume automatic checks.

Physical scale linking

  • Link scale matches physical magnification while moving each image independently.
  • Link scale + frame also links movement using the existing alignment.
  • The LUT panel now uses graph handles without Min/Max entry boxes.

macOS Apple silicon. Calibrated scale-bar exports remain available.

Calibrated scale-bar exports

  • Scale bar + SVG embeds a lossless PNG with an editable vector bar and label.
  • Scale bar + JPEG saves the selected image with a high-quality calibrated bar.
  • Both follow the region, channels, LUT, frame and export scale.

macOS Apple silicon. Physical comparison linking is planned for 2.1.4.

LUT range and live contrast

  • Full intensity range by default, with optional Auto-fit.
  • Scroll to zoom, drag or scroll sideways to pan, and double-click for the full range.
  • Live contrast updates while dragging, plus exact Min/Max entry.

macOS Apple silicon. Existing slides, annotations and viewing caches are preserved.
